rows.title: Address book list: Design Release 2.1 intro, filter disclosure, search control, table cells, empty state and a banner that stays
rows.detail: The INS address book list changes to Design Release 2.1's layout and copy. The intro is reworded and set in large body text, 'Add a new address' moves directly under it, and search moves into a collapsed 'Filter addresses' disclosure, a GOV.UK details component, with a plain 'Search' label, a placeholder instead of a hint and an icon-only search button that is a real submit button. The 'Clear search' link goes. The table shows a multi-word name on two lines and every stored address line on its own line. An empty book or a search with no match shows the same table with 'Showing 0 of 0' instead of a message, and the success banner stays until the user leaves or reloads the page, so its hiding script is removed. Every part works without JavaScript. All of this is the same list page and template, so it is one review.
acceptanceCriteria: Under the 'Address book' heading the list shows, in large body text, 'Manage your addresses for use across all your import notifications' in place of 'Manage addresses used across import and export services.' (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-005; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p16-003; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p6-083)
The 'Add a new address' button comes directly under the intro, above the 'Filter addresses' disclosure. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-006, prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-008)

The search field sits inside a 'Filter addresses' disclosure with a chevron, built on the GOV.UK details component and collapsed when the list loads, so the search field is hidden until the user opens it; it opens and closes with JavaScript off. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-008; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p6-085, prototype-dr2-1-specs-p6-099; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-046, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-098)

The search field is labelled 'Search', in place of 'Search addresses'. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-011; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p16-021; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p6-100)

The search field shows the placeholder 'Search by name, address or country' and has no hint. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-011; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p6-101)

The search field has an icon-only search button whose accessible name is 'Search', and no visible 'Search' text button; with JavaScript on or off, pressing that button, or pressing Enter in the search field, submits the search and the list shows its matches. (trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p16-021; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-047, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-099)
No 'Clear search' link shows, whether a search found addresses or found none. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-013-m1; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p16-022-m1)

When the book is empty, or a search matches nothing, the list shows 'Showing 0 of 0' and the table with its column headers and no rows; 'You have no addresses yet.' and 'No addresses match "<term>".' no longer show. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-029, prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-042; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p16-131)

In the Name column a name of more than one word shows on two lines, the first word then the rest, such as 'Green' then 'valley farm'; a one-word name shows on one line. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-032; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p16-016)

In the Address column each stored address line (line 1, line 2, town or city, county, postcode) shows on its own line, each but the last ending in a comma, with blank lines left out, so line 2 and county now show when they hold a value. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-033; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p16-017)

After an add, edit or delete the success banner is still showing 10 seconds after the list loads, and stays until the user leaves or reloads the page. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-007; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-097, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-100)

sources.ref: claim 6 (works without JavaScript; filters are forms with a submit button), claim 23 (banners stay), claim 24 (inc-063 details disclosure, submit button, banner script removed)

rows.notes: Combines three thin slices on the same list page and template: the heading area and search control (req-1112, 1114, 1115, 1116, 1117, 1118, 1133), the table cells (req-1136, 1137) and the empty state and banner (req-1132, 1147). Built apart they would repeat the same list template, copy file, fit spec and E2E page object for little gain. c-171 settled that the empty and no-match messages, the Clear search link and the timed banner go; Sam's 9 October afternoon ruling (claim 24) confirms the disclosure is the GOV.UK details component, the icon button is a real submit button of a GET form, and the INS frontend's success-banner hiding script is removed (WCAG 2.2.1). The Type select joins the 'Filter addresses' disclosure in the Type-filter row; until then the disclosure holds the search field alone. Filtering as the user types is not built in this programme: it waits on design question 5 in the waiting-on-design theme (req-2039, c-169), so here the search submits as a GET form only. Each new English string gets a Welsh machine draft as it is added; req-1186's completeness check is the Welsh row. The client entry file that loads the banner script is shared with other client scripts.

rows.title: View an address: GOV.UK page titles, optional rows only when filled, a secondary Edit button and no 404 for a dead link
rows.detail: The address book pages take Design Release 2.1's page titles, with the GOV.UK suffix and a hyphen separator. The view page leaves out an empty address line 2 or county, labels county 'County (optional)', styles Edit as a secondary button beside Delete, and sends a user who opens a dead address link (unknown, malformed, another organisation's or deleted) to the view page's back link instead of showing a 404 page.
acceptanceCriteria: The page titles read 'Address book - Import notification service - GOV.UK' on the list, '<address name> - Import notification service - GOV.UK' on the view page and 'Delete this address? - Import notification service - GOV.UK' on the delete page, in place of today's pipe-separated titles. (trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p16-001, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p16-101, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p16-118; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p6-081, prototype-dr2-1-specs-p6-151, prototype-dr2-1-specs-p6-166)

The view page shows the 'Address line 2 (optional)' row after Address line 1 only when the address has a line 2, and the county row after Town or city only when it has a county; neither shows blank. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-052)
The view page's county row is labelled 'County (optional)'. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-052)

The view page's 'Edit' button, to the address's edit page, is a secondary (grey) button, beside the 'Delete' button in one button group. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-054, prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-055; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p16-104; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p6-156)

Opening the view page for an id that is not a live address in the user's organisation's book (an unknown id, a malformed id, another organisation's address or a deleted address) takes the user to the address book list, with no 'Page not found' page. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-047)

sources.ref: src/server/app/features/address-book/view (repo-insfrontend-p2-033 to p2-036, p2-043 to p2-051)

rows.notes: Combines the view-page slices (req-1161, 1162, 1164, 1168), which share one controller, template and fit spec. req-1110 (titles for the list, view and delete pages) rides here because it is one copy change to the shared page-title pattern and the view page is its biggest part; it touches the list and delete controllers' title only. req-1168 sends a dead link to the view page's back link: until the return-path row lands that is always the list, and that row extends it to an honoured return. The not-live checks live in the shared address-id params and stored-address helpers, which the add-and-edit area's edit page also uses.

rows.title: Delete an address: Design Release 2.1 confirmation page, 'No, cancel' link, a stale delete as a no-op and the new banner
rows.detail: The delete page becomes Design Release 2.1's confirmation: the heading 'Delete this address?', a summary of the address being deleted, a confirmation line, a warning that it cannot be undone, a red 'Yes, delete' button and a 'No, cancel' link. A delete for an address that is no longer live redirects instead of showing a 404. After a delete the list's banner reads '<Name> address deleted'. The delete stays a soft delete through the address book API, which has no restore, so the warning is true.
acceptanceCriteria: The delete page's heading is 'Delete this address?', in place of 'Delete address'. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-088; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p16-118; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p6-167)

The delete page shows a summary list with one row, 'Address', holding the name, each address line and the country on separate lines, leaving out any line that repeats one already shown (ignoring case) and never showing the email or phone; with none of those it shows 'Not applicable'. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-089, prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-090; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p16-119; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p6-168)

Below the summary the delete page says 'Confirm that you want to delete this address.', and 'Are you sure you want to delete <name> from your address book?' no longer shows. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-091; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p16-120; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p6-169)

The delete page warns 'This action cannot be undone.' (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-091; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p16-121; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p6-170)

After 'Yes, delete' the list's banner reads '<Name> address deleted' with the name's first letter capitalised and the rest lower-cased, such as 'Green valley farm address deleted' for 'Green Valley Farm', or 'Address deleted' when the name is blank. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-095; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p16-124; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p6-173)

Opening the delete page for an id that is not a live address in the organisation's book takes the user to the address book list, with no 'Page not found' page; posting a delete for such an id changes nothing, shows no banner and lands on the list. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-086, prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-097)

They share one controller, template, fit spec and E2E page object. The delete stays a soft delete through the address book API, which already tombstones and has no restore (repo-addressbook-p2-064), so the warning is true. The redirect for a dead link goes to the list until the return-path row extends it to an honoured return. The tests repo's delete page object reads 'Yes, delete this address' today and changes with this row.

rows.title: View and delete pages return the user to where they opened the address from, including an animals journey page
rows.detail: A user who opens an address from somewhere other than the list, such as a live-animals or germinal products journey page in the animals frontend, goes back there. The view and delete pages honour a return query: an INS path, or an absolute URL on exactly the configured animals frontend origin. Anything else falls back to the list (view page) or the view page (delete page). The return parameter's name is the INS service's to choose, and the allow-list stays.
acceptanceCriteria: Opening the view page with a return that starts with a single /, such as the dashboard's path, makes its Back link go to that page, and its Edit and Delete links carry the same return on. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-048, prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-049, prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-055; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-092)
On the delete page reached that way, Back and 'No, cancel' go to the view page still carrying the return. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-092, prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-093)

After 'Yes, delete' the user lands on the return page, unless it is one of the deleted address's own pages, when they land on the address book list. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-096)

Locally, on the compose stack and in CDP, a return that is an absolute URL whose origin exactly equals that environment's animals frontend base URL is honoured: opening an address with a return to a live-animals journey page and pressing Back lands on that page. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-049; repo:tests repo-tests-p5-001)

Locally, on the compose stack and in CDP, a return to a germinal products page on that same animals frontend origin is honoured the same way, so Back lands on that germinal products page. (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-006; prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-049)

Any other return (another origin, one starting with //, or one not starting with /) is ignored: the view page's Back goes to the address book list and the delete page's Back and 'No, cancel' go to the view page. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-049; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-092)

In the INS frontend's stub mode only returns that start with a single / are honoured; an absolute animals frontend URL falls back as any other return does. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-049)
A dead view or delete link carrying an honoured return lands on that return rather than the list. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-047, prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-097)

sources.ref: ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-006 (germinal products set in the animals frontend); ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-092 (return parameter name is the service's, allow-list stays)

rows.notes: Kept apart from the view and delete rows because it carries a cross-origin, per-environment rule (c-170) the copy changes do not, and its own security review: the allow-list is exactly the animals frontend origin, never any origin, and never the plants frontend. Sam's 9 October ruling leaves the return parameter's name to the INS service and keeps the allow-list, so no criterion names the parameter. Germinal products is a set inside the animals frontend, so its pages share the allowed origin; the germinal criterion needs no germinal page to link into the book, only a return URL on that origin. Depends on the view-page row and the delete-page row (it changes the Back, Edit, Delete, 'No, cancel' and dead-link behaviour those rows settle). The INS config already holds the animals frontend base URL, so no new setting is expected. The last criterion completes req-1168 and req-1169's 'back link' fallback once a return exists.

rows.title: Address book list split into three category tabs with a Type column
rows.detail: The list is split by what each address is used for: three tabs, 'Origin and Consignor', 'Destination, Consignee and Importer' and 'Branch', drawn as the Ministry of Justice sub navigation component, each a link that loads the list on that tab, with its own panel heading. An address shows on every tab whose category holds one of its types, so the address book API learns to return one category's addresses. The tables gain a Type column with the address's type labels. The INS frontend adds the MoJ frontend package at the animals frontend's major version. The tests repo's shared address book fixtures carry a type so they land on the right tab and the journeys still find them, and the k6 performance suite's address book scenarios search and count per tab. The Transporter tab waits with transporter management.
acceptanceCriteria: The list shows three tabs in this order: 'Origin and Consignor', 'Destination, Consignee and Importer' and 'Branch', drawn as the Ministry of Justice sub navigation; each is a link that loads the address book list on that tab, with JavaScript on or off, and the selected one is marked. No 'Transporter' tab shows. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-022; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p6-086 to p6-089; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p16-006; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-103, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-104, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p2-045)

Each tab panel is headed 'Origin and Consignor addresses', 'Destination, Consignee and Importer addresses' or 'Branch addresses'. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-023; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p16-008, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p16-029; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p6-090)

Opening the address book with no tab chosen, or an unknown one, shows the Origin and Consignor tab selected. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-025; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p16-007; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-091)

An address shows on every tab whose category holds one of its types: Origin and Consignor holds place of origin, consignor, consignor or exporter and exporter; Destination, Consignee and Importer holds consignee, importer, place of destination, contact and packer; Branch holds branch addresses. An address held as both place of origin and consignee shows on both the first two tabs. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-024, prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-027; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p16-013; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-115)

The address book list API, asked for one category, returns only the caller's organisation's live addresses with a type in that category, paged as before. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-024; repo:addressbook repo-addressbook-p3-046; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-116)

On every tab the table's columns are Name, Type, Address and Country, then an action column whose header 'Action' is visually hidden. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-030; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p16-011; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p6-092)

The Type column shows the address's type labels joined by ', ', using 'Place of origin', 'Consignor' (for consignor, consignor or exporter and exporter), 'Consignee', 'Importer', 'Place of destination', 'Branch', 'Contact address' and 'Packer', such as 'Place of origin, Consignor'. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-034, prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-035; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p16-013 to trace-prototype-dr2-1-p16-015)

The tests repo's shared address book fixtures each carry a non-transporter address type, so each shows on its category's tab and the animals journeys' party pickers still find them; the pre-run reconcile reports a fixture with a missing or different type as drift and puts it right. (repo:tests repo-tests-p5-113, repo-tests-p5-117 to repo-tests-p5-121-m1)

Run against the local stack, the k6 performance suite's setup finds 'Perf Test Holding' by searching the tab its type lands on, adding it only when that search misses it, so a second run adds no duplicate; each address-book session's search for the address it has just added, and the worst-case search, ask for the tab their address's type lands on and find it. (repo:perftests repo-perftests-p2-023 to repo-perftests-p2-025, repo-perftests-p2-039; prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-025, prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-028; ruling:sam-2026-10-07 ruling-sam-2026-10-07-p1-002)

Run against the local stack, the k6 background-volume step counts the book by adding up the three tabs' results lines, its seeded addresses each carrying one non-transporter type so none is counted twice, and the run leaves no address it added behind in the book. (repo:perftests repo-perftests-p2-026, repo-perftests-p2-046; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p2-045)

rows.gate: Look at the MoJ sub navigation tabs, the category-to-type mapping and the list API's category filter before the Type filter, search and (once unblocked) Transporter-tab rows build on them.
rows.notes: Rewritten for Sam's 9 October afternoon ruling: three tabs, not four (claim 36: the Transporter tab, its heading, its Type label and its columns wait with transporter management, req-2040, in the blocked Transporter-tab row), and the tabs are MoJ sub navigation, each a link that loads the page, with the INS frontend adding @ministryofjustice/frontend at the animals frontend's major version (claims 7 and 26, c-304). Combines the tab slices (req-1123, 1124, 1125, 1126), the Type column (req-1134, 1139) and the typed fixtures (req-1187): all rest on the same new category filter and the same list template, and the fixtures must be typed in the same change or the E2E specs that find them break. Sam's 9 October ruling (c-253) leaves the tab parameter's name and values to the INS service, so the criteria assert the tab shown, never a query string; the search parameter keeps q. How the record and the API carry type and category is the address book service's design. Real ordering need on another area: the address book record must carry its types first, which is the address-book-add-and-edit area's typed-record row (inc-059, req-1256). The tab links' search-keeping and Type-dropping (req-1127) are in the Type-filter row. The in-memory stub learns the category filter here as far as the fit suite needs; req-1185 is closed by the search row. The k6 suite searches and counts the whole book on one list; once a search and the results line cover only the selected tab, a search on the default tab misses an address of another type, so c-225 puts the suite's change (req-1861) in this row, on its branch name; every route and hook the suite reads is kept (req-1860, already met). Adding the MoJ package touches the INS frontend's package manifest, its Nunjucks search paths and its stylesheet entry, which other areas may also change. Gate set because the following rows copy this pattern.

rows.title: Type filter within a category tab, with tab and pagination links that keep the user's filters
rows.detail: Inside the 'Filter addresses' disclosure a 'Type' select narrows the current tab to one type, across the whole category rather than just the page, on the server. Changing the select submits nothing by itself: the search button or Enter submits the filter form, which works without JavaScript. Tab links keep the search but drop the Type, which is per category, and pagination keeps the tab, search and Type.
acceptanceCriteria: The 'Filter addresses' disclosure holds a select labelled 'Type' whose first option is 'Select one' (no value), then the current tab's options only: 'Place of Origin' and 'Consignor' on Origin and Consignor; 'Consignee', 'Importer' and 'Place of Destination' on Destination, Consignee and Importer; 'Branch Address' on Branch. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-013 to prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-016; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p16-022, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p16-023, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p16-025; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p6-093)

Choosing a Type and pressing the search button, or Enter on the select, keeps, across the whole category and not only the current page, the organisation's live addresses one of whose types equals the choice, and drops the rest; with JavaScript on or off this works the same. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-017; repo:addressbook repo-addressbook-p3-046; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-116, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-118; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-047)
Changing the Type select on its own does not reload or change the list. (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-061, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-101)

Filtering keeps the user on the tab they are on: the tab stays selected after a search or Type choice is submitted. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-009, prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-010)
Each tab link opens page 1 of that tab, keeps the current search and drops the Type. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-028)
Pagination links keep the tab, search and Type, and add a page number only for pages after the first. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-040; trace:ins-fit trace-ins-fit-p2-027)

Kept apart from the tabs row so that row stays reviewable and its gate lands first. The Transporter tab's 'Commercial' and 'Private' options and matching on a transporter's type wait with that tab (req-2041), so they are not here. The tab and type parameters' names are the INS service's (c-253), so no criterion names them. Depends on the category-tabs row.

rows.title: Search the whole row, 8 addresses a page, a list that clamps stale page numbers and a stub that behaves like the real book
rows.detail: Search finds an address by anything the row shows: name, type labels, every address line and country, not only name, town and postcode. The list pages at 8 through the address book service's server-side page size setting. The filter stays a GET form that the search button or Enter submits, working fully without JavaScript, and nothing re-requests the list as the user types. A stale page number shows a real page. The INS frontend's in-memory stub behaves the same, so the fit suite exercises the Design Release 2.1 list, and the E2E specs walk the address book through its own links.
acceptanceCriteria: Search matches the trimmed text, ignoring case and anywhere inside a word, against an address's name, type labels, address line 1, address line 2, town or city, county, postcode and country name, so 'ballymore' finds an address whose line 2 is 'Ballymore Road' and 'france' finds the addresses in France; a blank search is no search. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-018 to prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-021; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p16-026; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p6-102, prototype-dr2-1-specs-p6-103)

Locally, on the compose stack and in CDP the list shows 8 addresses a page, with no page-size parameter on the request: the address book service's server-side page size is 8. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-038; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p16-010; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p6-091; repo:addressbook repo-addressbook-p3-011)

Locally, on the compose stack, in CDP and in the INS frontend's stub mode, with JavaScript on or off, pressing the search button or Enter in the search field or on the Type select reloads the address book list on the same tab with that search and Type applied, and the list shows that tab's matches across all its pages. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-013-m1; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-091; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-047, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-072)
Typing in the search field sends no request and does not change the list until the search is submitted. (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-061, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-072)

While a search or Type filter is active the results line counts the matches, such as 'Showing 1-2 of 2', and pagination shows only when the matches run past one page of 8. (trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p16-027; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-072)

A page number below 1 or not a number shows page 1, and a page number beyond the last page shows the last page's addresses rather than an empty table. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-041)

In the INS frontend's stub mode the list behaves the same: 8 a page, filtered by search, tab and Type, and a deleted address reads back as deleted rather than vanishing. (repo:insfrontend repo-insfrontend-p2-078, repo-insfrontend-p2-079, repo-insfrontend-p2-081)

The E2E specs reach every address book page through the list's own links (list, category tab, search, View, Delete, 'No, cancel', 'Yes, delete') rather than by URL, and cover the empty and no-match state. (repo:tests repo-tests-p5-102, repo-tests-p5-109-m1; repo:insfrontend repo-insfrontend-p2-106; trace:e2e trace-e2e-p15-039)

Filtering as the user types, which an earlier version of this row carried, is its own increment blocked on design question 5 in the waiting-on-design theme (req-2039), which depends on this row; c-169's earlier re-request-as-you-type outcome is replaced. rows.title: Transporter tab: transporters listed with approval number and type, filtered and searched
rows.detail: Once transporter management is decided, the address book gains a fourth tab, 'Transporter', between 'Destination, Consignee and Importer' and 'Branch', listing the organisation's transporter entries with Design Release 2.1's columns: Name, Address, Approval number and Type, with the country as the address's last line. It waits on the product owner's decision on whether the service manages transporters and, if so, in the address book.
acceptanceCriteria: On the Transporter tab the table's columns are Name, Address, Approval number and Type, then the visually hidden Action column, with no Country column; the country shows as the address's last line, the approval number reads like 'RO/BUCHAREST/T1/00092010' and Type is 'Commercial' or 'Private'. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-031, prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-036; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p16-032 to trace-prototype-dr2-1-p16-035; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p6-098)
A transporter added to the address book shows on the Transporter tab and on no other tab. (trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p16-132; prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-031)

rows.title: Welsh for the redesigned address book list, view and delete pages
rows.detail: Every new or changed English string on the address book list, view and delete pages has a Welsh counterpart, marked as an unreviewed machine draft until it has Welsh Language Standards sign-off, so a Welsh user sees the same Design Release 2.1 page rather than today's. The Welsh for the Transporter tab waits with that tab.
acceptanceCriteria: With Welsh selected, the list, view and delete pages show a Welsh string for every piece of copy the Design Release 2.1 rows added or changed (intro, 'Filter addresses', 'Search', the placeholder, the three tab names and headings, column headers, Type labels and options, 'County (optional)', 'Delete this address?', 'Confirm that you want to delete this address.', 'This action cannot be undone.', 'Yes, delete', 'No, cancel', the banners and the page titles), and no English string is left. (repo:insfrontend repo-insfrontend-p2-098; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p2-047)

Today's Welsh strings for the replaced copy, such as 'Rheoli cyfeiriadau a ddefnyddir ar draws gwasanaethau mewnforio ac allforio.', 'Chwilio cyfeiriadau' and 'Dileu cyfeiriad', no longer show. (repo:insfrontend repo-insfrontend-p2-099 to repo-insfrontend-p2-105)
Each new Welsh string is visibly marked, where the Welsh copy is kept, as an unreviewed machine draft awaiting Welsh Language Standards sign-off. (repo:insfrontend repo-insfrontend-p2-098)

sources.ref: claim 36, third bullet (inc-083 no longer depends on inc-075; Transporter Welsh waits)

Builders of the earlier rows add a Welsh machine draft beside each English string they add, so the Welsh page never falls back to English for long; this row completes and verifies it. Sam's 9 October afternoon ruling (claim 36) takes the dependency on the blocked Transporter-tab row away: the Welsh for the Transporter tab waits with that tab. Depends on every buildable row in this area: the list row, the return-path row (and through it the view and delete rows) and the search row (and through it the tabs and Type-filter rows).

rows.title: The address types offered when adding an address
rows.detail: The type choices Design Release 2.1 offers when adding an address, in order and with their hints, which also name the categories the list's tabs and Type filter group by. The choice itself is made on the add-and-edit area's type step, so this requirement belongs in that step's row.
acceptanceCriteria: The address types offered when adding an address read, in this order and with these hints: 'Place of Origin' ('The address where the animals begin their journey to Great Britain'), 'Consignor' ('This is the sender of the consignment.'), 'Consignee' ('This is the receiver or buyer of the consignment being shipped or transported.'), 'Importer' ('This is usually the same as the consignee. You can select a different person if needed.'), 'Place of Destination' ('This is where the animals will be unloaded and accommodated for at least 48 hours. If a health certificate is required, it will show this address.'), then, after a divider, 'Branch Address' ('This is the contact address of the person responsible for the consignment from when it enters Great Britain until authorities complete their checks.'); no 'Transporter' type is offered. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-105 to prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-111; repo:tests repo-tests-p5-095; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p2-046)
